content:
Overview # Statistics is a mathematical science concerned with collecting, analysing, interpreting and presenting empirical data. Research in statistics develops theory and methods for extracting information from data, quantifying uncertainty, making predictions and supporting decisions in the presence of randomness.
Statistical Modelling and Inference is central to modern statistical science. Research in this field develops theoretical frameworks and probabilistic models for representing real-world phenomena and drawing valid conclusions from observed data. It also develops mathematical methods, algorithms and estimators for inference and uncertainty quantification. Major areas include regression analysis, generalized linear models, multivariate data analysis and nonparametric statistics.
Research Themes # The scope of statistics ranges from general statistical methodology to specialized applications across scientific fields. CENTAUR focuses on the following research themes.
Bayesian Statistics # Bayesian methods use probability to represent uncertainty and combine prior information with observed data. Research includes computational methods such as Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) for inference in complex multiparameter models.
Statistical Learning and High-Dimensional Data Analysis # This theme develops algorithms that learn from data to identify patterns, classify observations and make predictions. Research addresses theoretical guarantees, scalability, interpretability, uncertainty quantification and variable selection in settings where the number of variables may far exceed the number of observations.
Computational Statistics and Numerical Methods # This theme lies at the intersection of statistics and computer science and develops numerically stable and efficient algorithms for data analysis. Research includes optimization methods such as the EM algorithm, numerical integration, stochastic simulation and parallel computing for likelihood-free inference and computationally intensive model estimation.
Nonparametric and Semiparametric Methods # This theme studies statistical models that avoid restrictive finite-dimensional parametric assumptions. Research includes the asymptotic theory of nonparametric estimators, empirical processes and semiparametric efficiency bounds.
Biostatistics # Biostatistics applies statistical methods to medicine, biology and public health. Research includes clinical trial design, longitudinal data analysis, survival analysis, genomic data analysis and modelling the spread of infectious diseases to support reliable scientific and clinical conclusions.
Causal Inference # Causal inference develops methods for estimating cause-and-effect relationships rather than describing associations alone. Research includes the design of observational studies, counterfactual modelling, adjustment for confounding and estimation of causal effects when randomized controlled trials are infeasible.
Time Series and Spatial Analysis # This theme develops statistical models and methods for observations collected sequentially over time or across geographical space. Because such observations are often dependent, research develops models such as ARIMA models and Gaussian processes to represent temporal and spatial correlation and forecast future outcomes.
Econometrics # Econometrics applies statistical methods to economic data to study empirical economic relationships. Research addresses challenges including endogeneity, simultaneous equations and policy evaluation through specialized regression methods and instrumental variables.

content:
Overview # Data Science is an interdisciplinary field concerned with extracting information and knowledge from complex structured and unstructured data. It combines mathematical statistics, scientific methods, data-driven algorithms, scientific computing and computer systems to address scientific and practical problems.
Research Themes # CENTAUR studies the theoretical and applied dimensions of statistical data science through the following research themes.
Data Analytics and Visualization # This theme develops methods for the exploratory analysis of heterogeneous datasets to identify patterns, anomalies and structural behaviour. Research also examines graphical representations, including interactive dashboards and multidimensional visualizations, that make complex analytical results easier to interpret and use in scientific and organizational decisions.
Statistical Learning and High-Dimensional Data Analysis # This theme combines statistical inference with computational algorithms to develop predictive and explanatory models with guarantees concerning accuracy, stability and interpretability. Research studies empirical risk and generalization from finite training samples to unseen data. It includes regularization and sparsity methods, dimensionality reduction, manifold learning, resampling and model validation.
Computational Statistics and Optimization # This theme develops numerical tools for implementing complex statistical models at scale. Research includes optimization of constrained objective functions, methods for intractable probability distributions, stochastic optimization, simulation, and the design of deterministic and stochastic algorithms.
Scientific Computing # Scientific computing combines mathematical modelling, numerical analysis and software design to address large-scale scientific and engineering problems. Research examines high-performance implementation, data integrity and algorithms for parallel architectures, with emphasis on reproducibility, numerical stability and scalability.
title: Data Science

content:
Overview # Machine Learning is a subfield of artificial intelligence and computer science that develops mathematical algorithms and statistical models through which computational systems improve their performance using data and experience. It formulates prediction, classification and generation as optimization and statistical estimation problems rather than relying exclusively on explicitly programmed rules.
Research Themes # Research in Machine Learning at CENTAUR covers the following learning paradigms and specialized methodologies.
Supervised Learning and Predictive Modelling # Supervised learning estimates relationships between input variables and labelled outputs. Research examines the balance between model complexity and generalization in classification and regression. Methods include parametric and nonparametric models, support vector machines, ensemble methods such as random forests and gradient boosting, and deep neural networks for predicting categorical or continuous outcomes.
Unsupervised and Representation Learning # This theme studies unlabelled data to identify latent structure, probability distributions and informative features. Research in clustering and density estimation includes Gaussian mixture models and hierarchical clustering for high-dimensional data. Representation-learning methods, including self-supervised neural networks and autoencoders, seek lower-dimensional representations that retain relevant information.
Deep Learning and Neural Architectures # Deep learning uses multilayer neural networks to represent complex patterns in data. Research examines convolutional neural networks for spatial data, recurrent neural networks and transformers for sequential data, and graph neural networks for non-Euclidean structures. It also studies optimization and training dynamics, including convergence, vanishing or exploding gradients, dropout and batch normalization.
Reinforcement Learning and Sequential Decision Making # Reinforcement learning studies how agents select actions in dynamic environments to maximize cumulative reward. Research uses Markov decision processes to model sequential stochastic control and develops methods such as deep Q-networks and policy gradients for complex, high-dimensional state spaces. Applications include robotics, autonomous systems and game theory.
Trustworthy, Generative and Explainable AI and Applications # This theme studies the development, validation and application of advanced artificial-intelligence models. Research in generative AI develops methods for producing new data representations for scientific modelling. Research in trustworthy and explainable AI develops interpretable and uncertainty-aware explanations, examines their reliability and robustness, and addresses security and systematic bias.
Cross-domain applications include healthcare, such as medical imaging and genomics; finance, including risk assessment and fraud detection; and smart infrastructure, including climate forecasting and energy-grid management.

CENTAUR is a research laboratory of the Section of Statistics and Operations Research within the Department of Mathematics at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens. Its research spans Statistics, Data Science, Operations Research, Machine Learning, and Applied Probability, with emphasis on both the mathematical foundations and the application of methods in these areas.
The laboratory aims to promote inter-institutional and international research collaboration and is open to interdisciplinary partnerships within the framework of research and academic projects. It is also interested in collaborations addressing methodological and quantitative problems arising in industry and other applied settings.

content:
Academic Collaborations · Applied Research Partnerships
Academic Interdisciplinary & Research Collaborations # At CENTAUR, we believe that the most impactful scientific breakthroughs are born at the intersection of different disciplines. Specializing in the Mathematical Foundations and Applications of Statistics, Data Science, Operations Research, Machine Learning, and Applied Probability, our laboratory provides the necessary framework to support and enhance the quantitative and computational aspects of research across diverse scientific fields. We extend an open invitation to faculty members, research groups, and laboratories within NKUA and beyond to build strong interdisciplinary bonds and jointly tackle contemporary research challenges.
Areas of Collaboration & Synergies
Quantitative & Computational Research Support: We contribute to the development of advanced statistical models, machine learning algorithms, and optimization methods for analyzing data and simulating complex systems (e.g., in Medicine, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Informatics, Pharmacy, and Geology). Joint Research Proposals: We co-design and participate in funding proposals for national and international research programs, strengthening the interdisciplinary character of our University’s submissions. Co-organization of Academic Activities: We welcome the opportunity to co-organize seminars, workshops, summer schools, and joint research meetings that promote knowledge dissemination. Co-supervision & Researcher Exchange: We encourage the co-supervision of master’s theses and doctoral dissertations on topics of mutual interest, offering young researchers a fertile, cross-disciplinary environment. Applied Research Partnerships # At the CENTAUR Laboratory, we believe that connecting advanced academic research with the needs of the economy, public administration, and society can serve as a catalyst for innovation, growth, and improved decision-making.
With expertise in Statistics, Data Science, Operations Research, Machine Learning, and Applied Probability, our laboratory provides the mathematical foundations and modern computational tools required to address complex quantitative problems across a wide range of sectors and application domains.
We extend an open invitation for collaboration to businesses, industrial and professional bodies, start-ups, public organisations, public-interest and non-profit bodies, and other organisations interested in making effective use of quantitative methods and data. These collaborations may be research-oriented or applied in nature.
How We Can Collaborate
Specialised Problem Solving: The challenges faced by businesses and organisations can be translated into appropriate mathematical and statistical models, leading to practical solutions for process optimisation, trend forecasting, and data-driven decision-making.
Joint Research Projects: CENTAUR’s scientific expertise can be combined with the practical experience, data, and needs of partner organisations to develop research synergies and participate jointly in national and European funding programmes.
Development of Tailored Models and Methods: We develop statistical models, Machine Learning methods, and Operations Research algorithms tailored to the needs of specific applications. Indicative fields include finance, healthcare, energy, transportation, and supply-chain management.
Knowledge Transfer and Scientific Consulting: We provide scientific support for evaluating, designing, and improving the quantitative methods, analytical tools, and decision-making processes used by partner organisations.
